lesson: If you send the problem email to 25 people, nobody owns it. Name one person or it will not get done.
detail: On large projects everyone assumes someone else is handling it. Named individual accountability is the only fix he has found.

lesson: Write the commissioning schedule assuming it will be cut, because every week and dollar lost upstream gets taken from the end.
detail: Base build loses two weeks, pull it from commissioning. Budget loses a million, pull it from commissioning. By startup you are a dollar late and a day short.
role: Director of Commissioning, QTS Data Centers

lesson: Tell the customer what your product will not do before they find out on a jobsite. Honesty outsells features.
detail: Decades of overpromising vendors have construction workers' shields permanently up, so stated limits are the only thing that earns trust.
role: Product Evangelist and Construction Tech Advisor

lesson: Never introduce a new tool and a new process in the same rollout. One is change management; both is a multi-year slog.
detail: Granite maps every candidate solution against existing processes first, specifically to keep change management to one variable.

lesson: Help the electrician solve the problem on site today and he will not hit you with a change order tomorrow.
detail: Working with a trade to avoid ripping out work creates reciprocity that quietly eliminates future change orders.
role: Director of Facilities and Engineering, The Fresh Market

lesson: Forty-five checklists completed within two minutes of each other is a pencil-whipping signature the data will expose later.
detail: Pencil-whipped Level 2 checklists cascade into Level 3 and Level 4 delays. It is almost always ignorance rather than malice, so the fix is mentoring.
role: Director of Commissioning, QTS Data Centers

lesson: Create value for the person two levels above you and advancement takes care of itself.
detail: Career advice carried from Special Forces into construction: think about your boss's boss and make your work visibly useful to them.

lesson: If the GC super walks the site with his harness strap undone, every trade will too. Injuries trace back to the example you set.
detail: Quality and safety culture flow from the GC superintendent's own behavior. The goal state is a laborer calling out the super for missing gloves.

lesson: Put field practitioners on your advisory board, not just VPs, or you will build for the person who signs and not the one who uses.
detail: The people who detect BS are the ones who walk the site daily.
role: Product Evangelist and Construction Tech Advisor

lesson: Experienced workers' knowledge is walking out the door and there are roughly five years left to capture it digitally.
detail: The urgency is the retirement clock, not the technology.
role: Product Evangelist and Construction Tech Advisor

lesson: Walk the constructability with the foreman face to face. A short email is where a generation hides from hard conversations.
detail: Technology gets used as a buffer against accountability, because challenging someone over email is easier than in person.
role: Director of Facilities and Engineering, The Fresh Market
